## What this audit did not check

An audit that hides its blind spots manufactures false confidence, so:

- Only **row-wise formula patterns** are checked. A model where every cell
  in a row is legitimately different has nothing for Plumbline to compare
  against, and nothing here should be read as clearing it.
- **Whether the model is the right model** is not assessed. Plumbline checks
  internal consistency, not whether the business logic is correct.
- Cells using `OFFSET` or `INDIRECT` are excluded, because they build
  references while the workbook runs and cannot be analysed statically.
- 27 of 28 typed constants sitting
  among formulas were set aside as ordinary data rather than frozen
  formulas, because their values do not match what the surrounding
  formula would produce.
- A typed-in value is only reported when the formulas it is compared against
  sit in the **same block** of its row. That is what stops a data column being
  measured against a formula block elsewhere in the row, and it has a known
  cost: where **two or more adjacent cells** were overwritten, or where a whole
  block was, there is no surviving formula nearby to compare against and the
  cell is not reported. Wide, contiguous damage is the case this misses.

**A qualified reviewer should confirm each finding before any change is
made.** Plumbline does not edit workbooks and has not modified this one.
